[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Aligned Data Centers is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, led by CEO Andrew Schaap. As of this research date the company is mid-transaction: previously owned by private infrastructure funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management, it was the subject of an October 15, 2025 announcement in which the AI Infrastructure Partnership, MGX, and BlackRocks Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire all its equity at an approximately $40 billion enterprise value, reported as the largest data center transaction on record, with closing expected in the first half of 2026. This entry does not confirm whether that transaction has actually closed.

The companys current site describes 87 data centers under management and future development across 51 campuses, with 6.4 gigawatts of operational and planned capacity, and states its North American operations are 100 percent load matched with renewable sources. The October 2025 press release cites a slightly different snapshot, 50 campuses and more than 5 gigawatts, both figures recorded here rather than reconciled to one number. A flagship project, Project Caprock, is described as a sustainable 540 megawatt next-generation campus in Northwest Texas.

The registry here tracks 7 Aligned facilities across three states, Illinois, Texas, and Virginia, a small subset of the companys ten named North American markets, which also include Maryland, Atlanta, Ohio, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, and Hillsboro, Oregon, plus four Latin American countries. Aligneds stated multi-gigawatt capacity and pending $40 billion ownership change make it one of the largest single transactions recorded across any operator in this registry, and its research_status here should be revisited once the AIP/MGX/GIP acquisition closes. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as Aligned Energy Data Center in Phoenix, AZ, was not individually named in the operator-level research above, its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to Aligned based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

This session resolved facility specific detail for this Phoenix row. The operators own press release for this sites Phase II expansion states the address as 2500 W Union Hills, Phoenix, Arizona, and describes the existing campus at 51 acres with 550,000 square feet and 120 MW of power capacity, plus a Phase II expansion of 200,000 additional square feet at up to 60 MW at full build out, a 1.15 PUE, and rack densities up to 50 kW. The 200,000 square foot Phase II figure matches this rows already recorded technical_space_sqft. Because the 550,000 square foot and 120 MW figures describe the whole existing campus rather than a single confirmed operating building, they are recorded here in prose rather than applied to this rows critical_it_mw field. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service independently returned the identical street, 2500 W Union Hills Dr, Phoenix, AZ 85027, at 0.9 confidence, matching the operators own published address exactly. Given this exact match between the operators own tier one source and an independent coordinate based method, this session applies 2500 W Union Hills Dr, Phoenix, AZ 85027 as this rows address.

reading.body:
This facility publishes 200,000 square feet of technical space but no power capacity figure, making it impossible to assess its relevance to AI infrastructure or compare it to other Arizona data centers.

The operator's press release describes a Phase II expansion with a planned 1.15 power usage effectiveness ratio and rack densities up to 50 kilowatts per unit. These specifications indicate high-density design appropriate for compute workloads. Without a published megawatt figure, however, this site cannot place the facility in Arizona's mapped inventory or determine whether it serves AI tenants versus other workloads.

Arizona has 56 tracked facilities, but only four publish power capacity. This facility joins a larger pattern where operator disclosure varies widely. Size in square footage does not predict power draw or compute density, because cooling approach, voltage delivery, and rack configuration differ across data centers. A reader evaluating this campus would require the operator to publish IT load in megawatts before making siting or investment decisions.

The parent company, Aligned Data Centers, operates 87 facilities across 51 campuses with stated 6.4 gigawatts of capacity and is undergoing a $40 billion ownership transfer. The Phoenix expansion alone claims up to 60 megawatts at full buildout. Publication of this site-level capacity would clarify whether Aligned's portfolio growth is concentrated in a few large campuses or distributed across many smaller ones, which matters for understanding whether grid constraints bind differently by region.
